name: bluewater-21-busy-month
lines: This is Gus. He installs floors. And this is the best month he has ever had.
Every day is booked. The phone keeps ringing. He is turning work away.
Eleven weeks from now, his phone will not ring once.
He won't get a bad review. He won't make a mistake. He'll do what every busy owner does.
By the end of this video you'll know exactly what it was. And you have probably done it too.
Let's go back to the busy month. Gus is working six days a week.
A customer texts. Can I get a quote? He'll answer tonight. He doesn't.
He finishes a kitchen floor. The owner loves it. He means to send her the review link. He forgets.
He used to post a photo of every finished floor. This month, zero.
Every spring he texts his old customers. Not this spring. Too busy.
And honestly, it feels fine. The calendar is full. Why would he need marketing?
Here's the thing nobody tells you. Marketing works on a delay.
The call you got today did not start today.
It started weeks ago. Somebody saw a photo. Or read a review. Or heard your name from a neighbour.
Think of it like planting. What you put in the ground this month, you eat two or three months from now.
So his busy month was not made this month. It was made in the winter, when he was slow, and doing everything right.
And this month, he planted nothing.
Week three. Still busy. He's finishing jobs he booked a month ago.
Week six. Fewer new calls. He doesn't notice. He's still working.
Week nine. He finishes the last big job. He opens next week. It's empty.
Week eleven. The phone is on the counter. It has not rung since Monday.
So he panics. He boosts a post. He prints flyers. He drops his price.
And none of it works fast. Because the delay runs both ways.
What he plants today won't come up for weeks.
This has a name. Feast and famine. Most owners blame the season. Or the economy. Or luck.
It isn't any of those. It's the busy month.
So here's the fix. And it's smaller than you think.
Thirty minutes a week. The same thirty minutes. Even when you're slammed. Especially then.
One. Post one finished job. Ten minutes.
Two. Send the review link to every customer you finished that week. Five minutes.
Three. Text three past customers. Just checking in. Need anything before summer?
Four. Answer every quote request the same day. Even if the answer is, I'm booked until June.
That last one matters. Booked until June is not a no. It's a waiting list.
And a waiting list is what a slow month looks like, when you planned for it.
Now watch the same year again. Same busy month. But this time, thirty minutes a week.
Week eleven. The big jobs end. And the waiting list picks up the phone.
No panic. No price cut. No flyers at midnight.
We can't promise what your phone will do. Nobody honest can.
But we can tell you when a slow month gets decided. It gets decided in the busy one.
So if you're slammed right now, good. This is the week to plant.
And if you'd rather hand the planting to someone else, that's the job of a marketing department. Bluewater Co.
